Hi Samir —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed next step so we keep momentum:  

Recap:
- Finlytics is focused on improving document summarization and SEC filing extraction latency while reducing cost per inference.
- Primary success criteria: 95th percentile latency under 450ms for short summaries (<=1k tokens), extraction accuracy >= 92% on the gold prompt set, and infra cost target <= $0.01/token for production workload.
- Internal stakeholders: you (Head of AI), Maya Rao (ML Eng), and Amit Desai (Platform).

Proposed next step:
- Schedule an evaluation kickoff (30–45 min) to align on the trial plan, success metrics, and the prompt/eval set we’ll use. Connor (Sales Engineer) will join to cover technical scope and infra requirements.

I’m available next week (week of May 24) on Tue/Wed afternoons PST. Do any of these windows work for you? If not, share a couple of options and I’ll coordinate.

I’ve attached a one-page draft trial plan and a sample kickoff agenda to make the meeting productive.

Thanks,

Quick answers to your questions:
- Hosted vs Dedicated: For the kickoff and initial eval we recommend hosted with a temporary dedicated reservation for the high-burst windows if you want strict throughput guarantees. Connor will explain trade-offs; we can provision a small dedicated pool for peak test windows during the trial.
- Prompt/sample set: 120 extraction + 200 summarization samples is an excellent starting point. For rollout we usually recommend adding 30–50 long-tail examples from production logs after the first run.

1) Introductions & success criteria (5)
2) Trial plan and measurement approach (10)
3) Data & prompt ingestion / security (10)
4) Infra & performance knobs (batching, quantization) (10)
